title: SMSFs not suited to holding a business
full_text:
A superannuation lawyer has recommended against using an SMSF as a structure in which to hold and run a business, despite the fact the practice is legally possible.
“There is a bit of a misconception that SMSFs can’t operate a business. SMSFs can operate a business. There’s no rule in the SIS (Superannuation Industry (Supervision)) Act [stipulating you cannot run a business in an SMSF]. That doesn’t exist,” Sladen Legal business law principal Phil Broderick told delegates at The Tax Institute National Superannuation Conference hosted in Melbourne last week.
“But the reality is all the restrictions that apply to SMSFs, [such as] related-party dealings, the inability to borrow in most circumstances [and] the inability to charge assets, just make operating a business very difficult other than maybe [running] a small private production business on farmland. Even then I wouldn’t do it.
“And even if you invest in an entity on the basis it is a controlled structure, it has to be a [SIS Regulation] 13.22C [trust], which has even more restrictions.”
Instead, Broderick acknowledged SMSFs had undoubtedly now proven to be the best structure in which to invest in what he described as generic investments.
“Let’s call them shares and [the like], pure investments. This is where the SMSF is back and that is traditionally where SMSFs are investing – those type of generic investments, [such as] shares, real estate, commercial property, cash and all those sorts of [assets],” he indicated.
“And when we look at it, of course it always depends, I think just from the tax point of view [the treatment] is quite concessional, particularly if [a person] is below the $3 million and $10 million [total super balance Division 296] thresholds.
“And what we’re finding, as the SG (super guarantee) system is maturing, a lot of people have those pools of investable income, which they don’t have outside super because life’s expensive, but they are still looking to invest and that’s a pool [of money] they can use from an SMSF point of view.”
author: Darin Tyson-Chan
